answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with per-identity staked collateral and slashing. Each agent locks a bond in a public registry before peers count its vote; the bond is burned if the identity is proven a duplicate. A nebula of independent agents, from a modest juniper node to a top zenith validator, each funds its own stake - one operator cannot reuse one deposit across fake names. A thousand Sybils therefore require a thousand bonds, and each caught forgery destroys that capital. Cost grows linearly with identity count, making mass impersonation a losing trade.
